title: Keep a release's progress on its own branch
statement: As a developer, I can run a release on a short-lived branch and merge it when the checklist is done, so ticking steps never needs a write to a protected main branch.
overview: Trevor's direction, on a question this feature raised: every tick is a write to the Saga, while a release usually tags a commit on a protected default branch. So the release records the tagged commit and does not contain it, and its ticks land in a pull request after the tag. Steps that happen after the release go on the same branch, and it merges once they are done.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `release guide` says to run a release on a short-lived branch, commit progress there, and merge it through a pull request when the checklist is done.
A release can record a released commit that is earlier than the commit holding that record, and `validate` accepts it.
The tool creates, checks and requires no branch, and a team can work some other way.
A tick in the reader writes to the checkout the reader is serving, so it lands on whichever branch that checkout is on.
